methods.label: Pair triangles with complementary heights
methods.explanation:
The four marked boundary segments of length \(1\) make useful triangle bases. Let \(O\) be the intersection of the two slanted segments. Join \(O\) to the top left and bottom right corners. This divides the shaded region into four triangles with disjoint interiors, each having one of those length-\(1\) segments as its base.

For the two triangles with vertical bases, the perpendicular heights are the horizontal distances from \(O\) to the left and right sides. These distances add to the rectangle's width, \(8\). Thus this pair has total area
\[
\frac12\cdot1\cdot8=4.
\]
For the two triangles with horizontal bases, the heights are the distances from \(O\) to the top and bottom sides. They add to \(5\), so this pair has total area
\[
\frac12\cdot1\cdot5=\frac52.
\]
Adding all four triangles, the shaded area is \(4+\frac52=\frac{13}{2}=6\frac12\) square units, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses only triangle areas and the perpendicular sides of a rectangle. Locating the intersection or solving equations is unnecessary.
